correctness.rationale: Both connection elements have order three, so each Cayley graph is a disjoint union of right cosets of a cyclic group of order three and hence of triangles. The standard character is the permutation character minus the trivial character, so its values are fixed-point counts minus one. A 3-cycle and a product of two disjoint 3-cycles therefore give sums 2(n-4) and 2(n-7). Uniqueness of the degree-(n-1) irreducible character turns these into distinct singleton BI invariants. The low cases n=7,8 are independently reconstructed from the hook-length formula in the packaged verifier, while the n>=9 uniqueness input is classical.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source defines BI-groups and explicitly asks which finite groups are BI-groups. Its predecessor is known to prove symmetric groups non-BI, but that does not imply the same for alternating subgroups. The final construction supplies an explicit uniform witness entirely inside A_n for every n>=7. Targeted database and literature searches found no alternating-group BI classification theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem settles an infinite classical family in an explicit finite-group classification question. Alternating groups A_n are nonabelian simple for n>=5, so the result supplies a uniform negative answer on a central simple-group family rather than on sporadic small examples. The witness is structurally economical: two valency-two Cayley graphs with identical triangle decomposition are separated by a canonical irreducible character.
